A provisional bar in the last minutes of the CANDIDATE window sits inside the numerator and outside a baseline that already ended ten minutes ago, so its revision is ONE-SIDED by construction. This run did the latter -- two fetches a minute apart, merged, disagreements resolved to the later read.

HONEST SCOPE, and it is what makes the audit credible: this changed NO decision today. The price clause failed outright, and 51% of baseline still fails the volume clause decisively. volume_clause_denominator_collapse.mechanism: The 2026-08-25 calibration rule correctly replaced a session-average denominator with a trailing-local one, because the opening hour's 254,448/bar made midday fires impossible. That fix is right and stays. What nobody checked is the other end: a trailing-local mean tracks a DECAYING tape downward, so as participation drains the bar to clear falls with it. In a pre-event vacuum the clause stops asking 'did participation arrive' and starts asking 'is this bar busier than the vacuum' -- which any drift back toward normal satisfies. The filter is self-fulfilling exactly when the tape is least informative.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.why_it_survived: Both denominator defects are invisible from outcomes and point in OPPOSITE directions, so neither is detectable by counting fires. A session-average baseline vetoes everything and looks like discipline; a collapsed local baseline confirms everything and looks like the filter finally working. The 15:30Z run predicted a clean fire would FAIL on volume and treated a volume-confirmed break as 'far more informative than usual' -- exactly backwards, and it was refuted fifteen minutes later. A run that inherits that framing reads a vacuum fire as high-conviction.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.detector: Report the candidate bar's volume in ABSOLUTE terms alongside the ratio, and test it against the session's OWN earlier baselines as well as the trailing-30 mean. Confirmation requires BOTH: at or above the trailing local mean AND not materially below the session's established bucket rate. A bar that clears the local baseline while sitting under the session's own typical bucket is baseline collapse, not participation -- decline it and say which of the two it was.
volume_clause_denominator_collapse.honest_scope: This changed no decision on the day it was found: the fire was declined on five independent merits (magnitude 0.044%, a mid-range level, both MAs overhead and untouched, ex-gap IV/RV 1.1697, no catalyst), and the follow-through reverted to 103% of baseline with price flat, so the trade was bad on the tape as well as on the filter. volume_clause_denominator_collapse.class: Same family as every denominator finding in CLAUDE.md: a constant or a window encoded an assumption about a moving thing, nothing errored, and the wrong behaviour was indistinguishable from the right one. Here the assumption was that a locally-calibrated baseline is always the conservative choice. It is not; it is conservative in a rising tape and permissive in a draining one.
